title: Modern Network Environments

header.html: 1.8 Summarize evolving use cases for modern network environments: software-defined network (SDN) and SD-WAN; Virtual Extensible LAN (VXLAN); zero trust architecture (ZTA); Secure Access Service Edge (SASE) and Security Service Edge (SSE); infrastructure as code (IaC); IPv6 addressing
the official CompTIA Network+ N10-009 exam objectives, version 4.0

html:
1SDN and SD-WAN

Software-defined networking (SDN) separates the control plane (decisions) from the data plane (forwarding) and centralizes control in a controller that devices follow.

SD-WAN applies SDN ideas to the wide area network:

Feature Meaning
Application aware Chooses a path by application (voice over the best link)
Zero-touch provisioning A new device configures itself from the central controller on power-up
Transport agnostic Works over any link: MPLS, broadband, cellular
Central policy management One place defines policy for all sites

2VXLAN

Virtual Extensible LAN (VXLAN) encapsulates layer 2 frames inside UDP/IP so a layer 2 network can span a layer 3 network. It uses a 24-bit VXLAN network identifier (about 16 million segments) instead of the VLAN limit of 4,094.

Use Meaning
Data center interconnect (DCI) Extends the same layer 2 segment between data centers
Layer 2 encapsulation MAC frames carried in IP packets

3Zero trust and SASE

Term Meaning
Zero trust architecture (ZTA) Never trust, always verify: no implicit trust from network location
Policy-based authentication Every request is checked against policy (user, device, context)
Authorization / least privilege access Grant only the access needed, for the shortest time
SASE (Secure Access Service Edge) Cloud service combining networking (SD-WAN) and security (firewall, secure web gateway, zero trust access)
SSE (Security Service Edge) The security half of SASE (without the networking)
Exam tip

. "No device is trusted just because it is inside the network" = zero trust. SASE = SD-WAN plus cloud-delivered security; SSE = only the security part.

4Infrastructure as code (IaC)

IaC manages network configuration through code instead of manual changes.

Concept Meaning
Automation Playbooks, templates and reusable tasks apply the same configuration everywhere
Configuration drift Devices change away from the intended configuration; IaC detects and corrects it (compliance)
Upgrades Rolled out by script consistently
Dynamic inventories The device list is built automatically from the environment
Source control Version control, a central repository, conflict identification, branching

5IPv6

Fact Detail
Size 128 bits, written in hexadecimal groups, for example 2001:db8::1; :: replaces one run of zeros
Why Mitigates IPv4 address exhaustion
Compatibility Dual stack (run IPv4 and IPv6 together), tunneling (carry IPv6 inside IPv4), NAT64 (lets IPv6-only hosts reach IPv4 services)
Addresses No broadcast; link-local fe80::/10; loopback ::1
Exam tip

. SD-WAN is the WAN version of SDN; VXLAN stretches layer 2 over layer 3; SASE adds security to SD-WAN.

Exam tip

. IPv6 transition tools: dual stack (both), tunneling (IPv6 inside IPv4), NAT64 (IPv6-only to IPv4).

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A retailer wants new branch routers to configure themselves when plugged in, using central policy. Which technology fits?

  • ASD-WAN with zero-touch provisioning
  • BVXLAN with data center interconnect
  • CSpanning tree with root guard
  • DNetwork address translation
Show the answer

Answer: A. SD-WAN controllers provision devices automatically.

S2A company wants to extend a layer 2 segment across two data centers over an IP network. Which technology fits?

  • AVLAN trunking with native VLAN
  • BPort mirroring
  • CVXLAN
  • DNAT64
Show the answer

Answer: C. VXLAN carries layer 2 frames over layer 3.

S3A policy states that every access request is verified regardless of network location. Which model is this?

  • APerimeter-only security
  • BDemilitarized zone
  • COpen access
  • DZero trust architecture
Show the answer

Answer: D. Zero trust never assumes trust from location.

S4Network devices slowly drift from the approved configuration after manual changes. What helps most?

  • AA larger switch stack
  • BMore wireless access points
  • CInfrastructure as code with compliance checks
  • DA longer lease time
Show the answer

Answer: C. IaC detects and corrects configuration drift.

S5Which technology lets IPv6-only clients reach IPv4-only servers?

  • ADual stack
  • BNAT64
  • CAPIPA
  • DVXLAN
Show the answer

Answer: B. NAT64 translates between IPv6 and IPv4.

S6Which service combines SD-WAN with cloud-delivered security?

  • ASSE
  • BNFV
  • CSNMP
  • DSASE
Show the answer

Answer: D. SASE combines networking and security; SSE is only the security part.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What does SDN separate?

Show the answer

The control plane from the data plane.

R2How many bits is an IPv6 address?

Show the answer

128.

R3What does VXLAN encapsulate?

Show the answer

Layer 2 frames, inside UDP/IP.

R4What is configuration drift?

Show the answer

Devices changing away from the intended configuration.

R5What does dual stack mean?

Show the answer

Running IPv4 and IPv6 together.

R6What does least privilege mean?

Show the answer

Granting only the access that is needed.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
SDN / SD-WAN central controller; application aware, zero-touch, transport agnostic, central policy
VXLAN layer 2 over layer 3; DCI; 24-bit identifier
Zero trust / SASE never trust, always verify; SASE = SD-WAN + security; SSE = security
IaC playbooks and templates, drift, dynamic inventories, source control
IPv6 128 bits; dual stack, tunneling, NAT64
